text: Driftwood's Spring collection launch is about ten weeks out, the highest-traffic stretch of the year. Priya's worry is specific: last time, one VM was a single point of failure, and a bad moment during launch week shouldn't need a 2am phone call.

Casey's worry is different. Casey doesn't want infrastructure that only works because Theo remembers how he built it. Every piece should be describable in code and rebuildable by someone who wasn't in the room the first time.

Laid out side by side, each deliverable serves both people at once. Containers let orchestration restart a crashed instance automatically, and run the exact same image anywhere. Terraform lets infrastructure rebuild fast after a bad change, with no tribal knowledge required.

A CI slash CD pipeline runs tests before every deploy ships, and removes manual portal clicks entirely. The AWS backup target gives Priya a second copy of the app's data, and gives Casey a defined, auditable process instead of an ad hoc hope.

Theo writes a short scope document: containerize, Terraform, CI slash CD, and an AWS backup target are in. Migrating to AWS and Azure multi-region failover are explicitly out, for now. Lesson 3 starts the build with the Dockerfile.
